notes_on_text: The chapters have no titles; the titles in the contents of this edition are the editor’s, from what each chapter covers.
The French proclamation in Chapter X is given with its accents as printed, misprints included (“á ne pas”, “d’étre”).
summary: Patrick O’Brien, a young Irish member of Parliament, went from Constantinople to Wallachia in the autumn of 1853, when Russian troops occupied the Danubian Principalities and the Ottoman Empire had declared war on Russia, months before Britain and France joined the Crimean War. He goes up the Danube by steamer through quarantine at Ibraila and Galatz, crosses Wallachia by road, and lives at Bucharest through the early winter.

He describes Russian camps and reviews, the boyards and the peasants, and a night ride with despatches to Giurgevo past the Russian posts, and visits the field of Oltanitza after the battle. Several chapters set out the treaties and the government of the Principalities, and three turn to Greece, which he had known since 1843. He leaves over the Carpathians by Pesth to Vienna.
